### Computer Science & Engineering at MIT *(Officially part of the **EECS (Electrical Engineering & Computer Science)** department)* | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Department name** | **Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS)** – the world’s largest academic department at MIT. | | **Degrees offered** | **Undergraduate:**
• SB (Bachelor of Science) in Computer Science and Engineering (Course 6‑3).
• SB in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (Course 6‑2) (more hardware‑focused).

**Graduate:**
• SM (Master of Science) in EECS (research‑oriented).
• PhD in EECS (research‑oriented). | | **Core curriculum (undergrad)** |
  • **6.001** – Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (Python).
  • **6.002** – Circuits and Electronics (bridges CS & EE).
  • **6.003** – Signals and Systems.
  • **6.004** – Computation Structures.
  • **6.006** – Introduction to Algorithms.
  • **6.009** – Fundamentals of Programming.
  • **6.031** – Software Construction.
  • **6.036** – Introduction to Machine Learning.
  • **6.828** – Operating System Engineering.
| | **Key research areas** | • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (CSAIL, MIT‑IBM Watson AI Lab)
• Systems & Networking (CSAIL, CSAIL‑MIT Center for Digital Business)
• Robotics & Autonomous Systems (CSAIL, MIT Robot Locomotion Group)
• Theory of Computation & Algorithms (CSAIL, MIT Theory Group)
• Human‑Computer Interaction (MIT Media Lab, CSAIL)
• Security & Cryptography (MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, MIT CSAIL, MIT LIDS)
• Quantum Computing (MIT Center for Quantum Engineering)
• Computational Biology & Bioinformatics (MIT CSAIL & MIT Biology Dept.) | | **Major labs & centers** | • **CSAIL** – Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (largest CS research lab in the world).
• **MIT Media Lab** – Interdisciplinary work on interaction, design, and emerging tech.
• **MIT LIDS** – Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (systems, control, network science).
• **MIT‑IBM Watson AI Lab** – Joint AI research partnership.
• **MIT Center for Brains, Minds & Machines** – Cognitive science & AI.
• **MIT Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS)** – Data science & societal impact. | | **Notable faculty (selected)** | • Timothy **Berners‑Lee** (visiting professor, inventor of the World Wide Web – honorary).
• Yoshua **Bengio** (adjunct professor, deep learning pioneer).
• Regina **Barzilay** (NLP & AI, Turing Award‑candidate).
• David **Malcolm** (computer systems, operating systems).
• Anantha **P. Chandrakasan** (low‑power VLSI, EECS dean). | | **Reputation & rankings** | *U.S. News & World Report* consistently ranks MIT #1 in Computer Science (graduate) and #1–2 for undergraduate CS. The department is globally recognized for both depth and breadth of research. | | **Student life** | • **Undergraduate Association for Computer Science (UACS)** – events, hackathons, career talks.
• **MIT Hackathon (MIT Hacking Club)** – large‑scale 36‑hour hackathon.
• **Women’s Technology Program (WTP)** – summer outreach for high‑school girls.
• **Project Olympus, OpenCourseWare, MIT x** – many free online resources and open‑source projects. | | **Admissions (undergrad)** | • Highly selective: ~4–5 % acceptance rate for the overall MIT applicant pool; CS‑focused applicants compete with the most competitive high‑school profiles worldwide.
• Key factors: strong math & physics background, programming experience (often Python, Java, C++), compelling essays, and extracurriculars (e.g., research, competitions, open‑source). | | **Career outcomes** | • Top employers: Google, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Facebook/Meta, NVIDIA, Bloomberg, OpenAI, and many high‑impact startups.
• Median starting salary (2025 data) for EECS graduates ≈ **$135 k** (base) + bonuses/stock.
• Many graduates also pursue PhDs at top institutions or launch their own companies. | | **How to learn more** | • **MIT EECS website**: https://eecs.mit.edu/
• **MIT OpenCourseWare** for free lecture videos & notes (e.g., 6.006, 6.036).
• **CSAIL publications**: https://www.csail.mit.edu/publications.
• Admissions page: https://mit.edu/admissions. | | **Quick fun fact** | MIT’s **“6”** numbering system dates back to the original curriculum: **Course 6** is Electrical Engineering; the “3” suffix (6‑3) designates the Computer Science track that was split off in the 1970s. | --- #### TL;DR MIT’s CSE is housed in the massive **EECS** department, offering top‑ranked SB, SM, and PhD programs. It’s a hub for AI, systems, robotics, theory, security, and more, with world‑leading labs like **CSAIL** and the **Media Lab**. Admission is ultra‑competitive, but graduates enjoy stellar career prospects and a vibrant community of innovators.
